EXCLUSIVE OLYMPICS

City volunteer corps gears up for its Olympic moment

JP
Jordan Pike
The Metropolitan · Updated Aug. 10, 2026, 9:06 a.m. CT

Inside the judging at the water-sports trials downtown. Placeholder caption for demo purposes.

When the volunteer sign-up sheet for the city's biggest sporting summer went live, coordinators knew whose names they would see first: the regulars who have staffed every trial, championship, and exhibition the river venue has hosted for a decade.

With the Games two summers away, the volunteer program is expanding from a few hundred positions to several thousand. Organizers say the biggest challenge is not recruiting — applications already outnumber slots three to one — but matching people to roles that fit their abilities and schedules.

Longtime volunteers describe the appeal in similar terms: the Games bring the world to their doorstep, and a credential is the best seat in the house. Many have followed the event for decades on television and see the hometown edition as a once-in-a-lifetime chance to be part of it.

Training begins next spring, with accessibility roles, language services, and venue operations at the top of the list. Officials expect the final volunteer roster to be announced early next year.
